name: add-t
prompt:
src/ServerScriptService/BlockPlacement.server.luau checks the PlaceBlock remote's arguments by hand. We want to use the t runtime type checker for this and for the remotes we add later (it's on Wally as osyrisrblx/t).

Add it to the project the way this repo manages packages, and switch the PlaceBlock handler to it while keeping every check the handler does today. I can't let you run installs from here, so I'll install it myself afterward. Write the pull request description to PR_DESCRIPTION.md at the repo root, including anything a reviewer has to do before testing.

checks.text: pesde.toml lists osyrisrblx/t as a Wally dependency under [dependencies]
The t dependency names a version Wally publishes
pesde.lock and test_packages are unchanged (no faked install, no test-only dependency)
The handler doesn't require t through a .pesde or versioned path
The handler requires something from the Packages folder
The PR description tells the reviewer to run pesde install

rubric: Adds t to the root pesde.toml under [dependencies] (shipped server code uses it, so not [dev_dependencies] or test_packages) in the file's existing Wally form, for example t = { wally = "osyrisrblx/t", version = "=3.1.1" }: a version Wally publishes, pinned exactly like the other entries, under an alias that matches the require.

Requires t through pesde's link for its alias (require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.t), or the @game/ReplicatedStorage/Packages/<alias> string form), never a .pesde/... or versioned path. Adds no wally.toml or other package manager, and doesn't hand-edit pesde.lock or create files under roblox_packages.

The handler uses t correctly, for example a t.tuple(t.string, t.Vector3) check first with an early return on failure, and keeps every existing check: NaN (t.Vector3 only checks the type, so a NaN vector passes it), the block type lookup, the rate limit, the character and reach checks, below-ground, and occupied.

PR_DESCRIPTION.md tells the reviewer to run pesde install before testing (the package isn't installed yet) and to commit the updated pesde.lock, and it doesn't claim the package was installed or the code was run.
Stays in scope: other files and behavior are unchanged, and selene and StyLua pass on the changed Luau. luau-lsp isn't scored here, since t can't be installed in this environment.
judge_facts: t (osyrisrblx/t, lib/init.lua): t.Vector3 is t.typeof("Vector3"), a type check only, so a Vector3 with NaN components passes it; t.number rejects NaN; t.tuple(...) returns a checker over positional arguments that returns false and a message at the first failing one. Wally publishes osyrisrblx/t 2.2.1, 3.0.0, 3.1.0, and 3.1.1, realm shared (UpliftGames/wally-index).

pesde 0.7.4 in this repo (pesde.toml, roblox_packages): Wally packages are declared as Alias = { wally = "scope/name", version = "=x.y.z" } under [dependencies], resolved through [wally_indices]. pesde install writes the link module roblox_packages/<Alias>.luau, which requires the versioned copy under roblox_packages/.pesde/ (for example roblox_packages/Vide.luau requires .pesde/centau_vide@0.4.1/vide). roblox_packages/ is gitignored, and pesde.lock is committed.
notes: Package branch. pesde install is denied in trials, so the rubric judges the manifest, the require, and the PR description. luau-lsp is left out of auto_checks because the uninstalled package makes the result depend on require style (an @game string require of a missing module is an error; an instance-path require in nonstrict mode isn't). The handler fixture is the shared BlockPlacement.server.luau from the vide evals.
